1.explanation: The primary files likely responsible for this bug are the main Toggle implementations in both the vanilla and React component folders. These are: 'packages/components/src/components/toggle/toggle.js' for the vanilla JS implementation and 'packages/react/src/components/Toggle/Toggle.js' for the React implementation. The bug is directly tied to how aria-hidden is applied to the text elements in the Toggle component. Adjustments in these files are needed to ensure screen readers can access and announce the 'On'/'Off' labels as intended.
1.bug_scenario: The bug scenario concerns the accessibility of the Toggle component when used with screen readers, specifically VoiceOver. When users try to navigate and activate the toggle, VoiceOver does not announce the current label ('On'/'Off') as expected. Investigation (including the screenshot) reveals that the text labels are rendered with aria-hidden="true", which causes assistive technology to skip them, so users do not hear the toggle's status. Removing aria-hidden="true" allows the screen reader to read the labels, so the accessibility regression is tied to that attribute.
